newsitem.title: UK: Piracy attacks in Asia under-reported - claim.
newsitem.headline: Piracy attacks in Asia under-reported - claim.

text.p: The number of recorded pirate attacks on merchant ships fell in the first quarter of 1997 but the International Maritime Bureau (IMB) cautioned that raids, particularly in Asia, were grossly under-reported and details often slow to emerge.
The IMB Regional Piracy Centre said in its latest report, for the three months between January and March 31, 1997, that pirate attacks fell to 34 from 62 in the same period of 1996.
However, the Kuala Lumpur-based centre said: "Shipping companies in Singapore and port workers in Chittagong provide hard evidence that piracy is grossly under-reported."

"The attitude that nothing will be done so there is no point in reporting is understandable," and it added it "fully expects to receive details of more incidents in the coming months relating to the first three months of 1997."
The IMB reported that global piracy attacks rose to 224 over 1996 compared with 187 in 1995, after updating its figures with late reports.

It said the Bangladesh navy and coast guard agreed at the end of 1996 to patrol the port of Chittagong regularly after crews of coasters and lighter vessels refused to venture into the outer anchorage unless given adequate protection.
In Calcutta it said traffic has been restricted to daylight operations because of night attacks.

However, the IMB claimed some Singapore shipping companies were beginning to doubt the efficacy of joint patrols carried out by the navies of Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore after the hijacking of the Wint Thai No.1 and the theft of its cargo.
